verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the concrete spacing criterion that VELLVÉ must read as one cohesive wordmark rather than separated letter groups.
The client postpones full-wordmark construction and spacing work until the foundational V system is established.
The client explicitly resumes full-wordmark work, including evaluation of its rhythm and spacing.
The client establishes the L–V optical cadence as the spacing benchmark for all character pairs.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports first applying revised optical kerning based on the newly established L–V benchmark.
The client changes the wordmark spacing direction toward tighter optical spacing while preserving an uncompressed appearance.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports producing the requested standard and tighter kerning alternatives after the spacing change.
The client selects Variation B as the concrete tighter-kerning treatment for the wordmark.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports applying the client-selected Variation B kerning across every letter pair.
Post-claim failure: review of the rendered wordmark shows that it still reads as "VE | LL | VÉ" rather than one uninterrupted word.
The client replaces the prior kerning selection with a new comparison direction using progressively closer spacing; the removed selection key exists in prior state.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports creating three progressively tighter kerning stages in response to the observed grouped reading.
First concrete post-fix verification: after comparing the studies, the client reports that Option 2 reads as one unified word while retaining airiness and elegance.
The client establishes Option 2 (Balanced Flow) as the selected kerning configuration for the wordmark.
